title: Priests and Priesthood
lead: Priests stood between God and the people: they offered sacrifices, taught the law, sought God's decisions and blessed Israel. Aaron's family held the priesthood, assisted by the Levites. Melchizedek, Christ the high priest of Hebrews, and the "royal priesthood" of all believers (1 Peter 2:9) extend the theme.

sections.b: Before Sinai, Melchizedek (Genesis 14:18) and Jethro (Exodus 18:1) are priests of other peoples. Exodus 28–29 and Leviticus 8–10 found Aaron's priesthood, and Numbers 16–18 defends it against Korah and sets the Levites beside it as its helpers. Deuteronomy speaks of "the Levitical priests" (Deuteronomy 18:1). Eli's house falls (1 Samuel 2:27–36), Zadok's line serves Solomon (1 Kings 2:35), and Ezekiel limits the altar to the sons of Zadok (Ezekiel 44:15). Malachi rebukes careless priests (Malachi 2:1–9). After the exile the high priest leads the people (Zechariah 3). Hebrews presents Christ as a high priest in Melchizedek's line (Hebrews 7), and 1 Peter 2:9 and Revelation 1:6 call the church a priesthood.
